questions.stem: What is the default value for MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL on an Adaptive Warehouse?

options.text: MEDIUM
LARGE
XLARGE
XXLARGE

explanation.correct: The default MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL for an Adaptive Warehouse is XLARGE.

distractors.A: MEDIUM is not the default; it is a lower performance bound option.
distractors.B: LARGE is available but not the default value.
distractors.D: XXLARGE is above the default; it provides a higher performance bound.

questions.stem: What is the default value for QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER on an Adaptive Warehouse?

options.text: 0 (unlimited)

explanation.correct: The default QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER is 2.

distractors.A: A value of 0 means unlimited throughput but is not the default.
distractors.C: 4 is not the default; it must be explicitly set.

questions.stem: What is the minimum AUTO_SUSPEND value for an interactive warehouse?

options.text: 600 seconds (10 minutes)
3600 seconds (1 hour)
86400 seconds (24 hours)
300 seconds (5 minutes)

explanation.correct: The minimum AUTO_SUSPEND value for an interactive warehouse is 86400 seconds (24 hours) to ensure the cache stays warm long enough for consistent low-latency performance.

distractors.A: 600 seconds applies to standard warehouses but is far below the interactive warehouse minimum.
distractors.B: 3600 seconds is below the 24-hour minimum required for interactive warehouses.
distractors.D: 300 seconds is the default for standard warehouses but not applicable to interactive warehouses.

questions.stem: Which THREE properties are automatically managed by Adaptive Warehouses, eliminating the need for manual configuration? (Select THREE)

options.text: Suspend and resume policies
Multi-cluster warehouse settings
Query Acceleration Service settings
Warehouse size (XSMALL, SMALL, MEDIUM, etc.)
STATEMENT_QUEUED_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS
Resource monitors and budgets

explanation.correct: Adaptive Warehouses automatically manage warehouse size, multi-cluster settings, QAS settings, and suspend/resume policies. The question asks for three.

distractors.A: Suspend and resume policies are also automatically managed, but the question asks for three of the listed properties.
distractors.E: STATEMENT_QUEUED_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS can still be set on Adaptive Warehouses as an optional property.
distractors.F: Resource monitors and budgets are separate cost governance tools that still require manual configuration.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about interactive warehouses are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Interactive warehouses can query both standard tables and interactive tables
Queries exceeding 5 seconds are automatically cancelled on an interactive warehouse
Interactive warehouses support CALL commands for stored procedures
A fallback warehouse can be configured to automatically retry timed-out queries
Interactive warehouses use the same billing model as standard warehouses

explanation.correct: Interactive warehouses have a fixed 5-second statement timeout, and a fallback warehouse can be configured to transparently retry queries that exceed this limit.

distractors.A: Interactive warehouses can only query interactive tables; you must switch to a standard warehouse for standard tables.
distractors.C: You cannot run CALL commands to call stored procedures in an interactive warehouse.
distractors.E: Interactive warehouses have different billing (1-hour minimum on resume, per-second after) compared to the 60-second minimum for standard warehouses.

questions.scenario: A company wants to convert their existing standard warehouse to an Adaptive Warehouse without disrupting running queries.
questions.stem: Which SQL command performs this conversion?

options.text: CREATE ADAPTIVE WAREHOUSE my_wh CLONE my_standard_wh
ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh SET WAREHOUSE_TYPE = 'ADAPTIVE'
DROP WAREHOUSE my_wh; CREATE ADAPTIVE WAREHOUSE my_wh
ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh SET GENERATION = 'ADAPTIVE'

explanation.correct: ALTER WAREHOUSE with SET WAREHOUSE_TYPE = 'ADAPTIVE' converts a standard warehouse to Adaptive without downtime or interrupting running queries.

distractors.A: CLONE is not a valid syntax for converting warehouse types.
distractors.C: Dropping and recreating would cause downtime and lose the existing warehouse configuration.
distractors.D: GENERATION is used for Gen1/Gen2 standard warehouses, not for Adaptive type conversion.

questions.scenario: An administrator disables an Adaptive Warehouse using ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh DISABLE.
questions.stem: What happens to queries that are already running on the warehouse?

options.text: Running queries are immediately cancelled
Running queries continue to completion; only new jobs are rejected
Running queries are paused and can be resumed after enabling
The warehouse enters a suspended state and all queries queue

explanation.correct: When an Adaptive Warehouse is disabled, new jobs are rejected but queries already running can continue to completion.

distractors.A: Running queries are not cancelled; they complete normally.
distractors.C: Queries cannot be paused and resumed; they either complete or would need to be resubmitted.
distractors.D: DISABLE is different from SUSPEND; it specifically rejects new jobs while allowing current work to finish.

questions.scenario: A data platform team is creating an interactive table for their real-time dashboard that filters on a customer_id column.
questions.stem: Which TWO requirements must be met when creating this interactive table? (Select TWO)

options.text: The interactive table must be smaller than 1TB
A CLUSTER BY clause must be specified in the CREATE INTERACTIVE TABLE command
The table must be created using a standard warehouse, not an interactive warehouse
The table requires a PRIMARY KEY constraint
An interactive warehouse must already exist before creating the table

explanation.correct: Interactive tables are created using a standard warehouse (not an interactive one), and the CREATE INTERACTIVE TABLE command requires a CLUSTER BY clause specifying columns for query optimization.

distractors.A: There is no documented 1TB size limit for interactive tables.
distractors.D: No PRIMARY KEY constraint is required for interactive tables.
distractors.E: An interactive warehouse does not need to exist before creating the interactive table.

questions.scenario: A company has multiple Adaptive Warehouses: one for the finance team and another for engineering. They notice that all jobs across these warehouses draw from the same compute pool.
questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes this shared compute pool?

options.text: The pool is shared with other accounts in the same organization
The pool is shared with standard and interactive warehouses in the same account
The pool is dedicated to the account and not shared with other accounts or warehouse types
Each Adaptive Warehouse has its own isolated compute pool

explanation.correct: All Adaptive Warehouses in an account share a single pool of compute resources that is dedicated to the account — it is not shared with other accounts or used by other warehouse types like standard or interactive.

distractors.A: The pool is not shared across accounts in the organization; it is account-dedicated.
distractors.B: The pool is not shared with standard, interactive, or Snowpark-optimized warehouses.
distractors.D: Multiple Adaptive Warehouses in the same account share the same pool; they do not have isolated pools.

questions.scenario: An interactive warehouse has a table with 120TB of compressed data representing 1 year. The team mostly queries the last 7 days of data.
questions.stem: Based on the working set calculation, what warehouse size should they choose?

options.text: Small (600GB cache)
Large (2.5TB cache)
Medium (1.2TB cache)
X-Large (5.5TB cache)

explanation.correct: The working set is approximately 120TB / 365 days * 7 days = 2.3TB. A Large interactive warehouse provides approximately 2.5TB of cache, which fits this working set.

distractors.A: Small provides only 600GB of cache, far less than the ~2.3TB working set.
distractors.C: Medium provides 1.2TB of cache, which is smaller than the ~2.3TB working set.
distractors.D: X-Large provides 5.5TB, which is more than needed and would be unnecessarily expensive.

questions.scenario: A company wants to migrate all their standard warehouses matching a name pattern to Adaptive Warehouses. They want to preview the change before applying it.
questions.stem: Which function and execution mode should they use for the preview?

options.text: SYSTEM$BULK_UPDATE_WH with execution_mode 'DRY_RUN'
SYSTEM$MIGRATE_WAREHOUSES with mode 'PREVIEW'
SYSTEM$BULK_UPDATE_WH with execution_mode 'TEST'
SYSTEM$CONVERT_WAREHOUSE with mode 'SIMULATE'

explanation.correct: SYSTEM$BULK_UPDATE_WH with 'DRY_RUN' execution mode previews the migration without making changes, showing which warehouses would be affected.

distractors.B: SYSTEM$MIGRATE_WAREHOUSES is not a valid Snowflake function.
distractors.C: The valid execution modes are 'DRY_RUN' and 'ACTIVE', not 'TEST'.
distractors.D: SYSTEM$CONVERT_WAREHOUSE is not a valid Snowflake function.

questions.scenario: A team is evaluating whether to convert their standard Gen2 warehouse to an Adaptive Warehouse.
questions.stem: Which TWO workload characteristics make a warehouse a good candidate for Adaptive Compute? (Select TWO)

options.text: Mixed BI and ETL workloads with bursty, varied query shapes
Workloads primarily consisting of HTAP (hybrid transactional/analytical processing)
Workloads requiring very low latency for user-facing dashboard queries
Workloads with high size variance where queries range from XSMALL to XLARGE equivalent
High-memory Snowpark ML training workloads on a single node

explanation.correct: Adaptive Warehouses are ideal for mixed BI/ETL workloads with varied query shapes and workloads with high size variance where per-query resource allocation is beneficial.

distractors.B: Warehouses used primarily for HTAP should use standard Gen2 warehouses instead.
distractors.C: Very low latency for dashboards is better served by interactive warehouses.
distractors.E: High-memory single-node Snowpark workloads should use Snowpark-optimized warehouses.

questions.scenario: An administrator sets QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER to 0 on their Adaptive Warehouse.
questions.stem: What effect does this setting have?

options.text: The warehouse rejects all new queries
The warehouse has unlimited throughput with no cap on burst capacity
The warehouse operates at minimum throughput to reduce costs
The setting is invalid and generates an error

explanation.correct: Setting QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER to 0 means unlimited throughput — the warehouse can use as much burst capacity as available with no cap.

distractors.A: A value of 0 does not disable the warehouse; it removes the throughput limit.
distractors.C: A value of 0 means no limit, not minimum throughput.
distractors.D: 0 is a valid value; it represents unlimited throughput.

questions.scenario: A team has added an interactive table to their interactive warehouse and notices queries are slow immediately after resuming the warehouse.
questions.stem: Which TWO factors explain the slow initial performance? (Select TWO)

options.text: The data cache needs time to warm after the warehouse resumes
Interactive warehouses require a software update on each resume
Cache warming speed depends on warehouse size and table size
The interactive table must be re-created after each warehouse resume
Interactive warehouses require network reinitialization on resume

explanation.correct: After resuming, the data cache needs warming which causes initially slow queries. Warming speed depends on warehouse size (bigger = faster) and table data size (bigger = longer).

distractors.B: No software update occurs on resume; the issue is purely cache-related.
distractors.D: Interactive tables persist independently; they do not need re-creation after warehouse resume.
distractors.E: Network reinitialization is not a documented factor in interactive warehouse resume latency.

questions.scenario: A company converts their standard warehouse to Adaptive and wants to understand how billing works.
questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the Adaptive Warehouse billing model?

options.text: You are charged a fixed hourly rate based on MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL
You are charged per query based on compute and software resources used
You are charged per cluster-hour similar to multi-cluster warehouses
You are charged only when QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER exceeds its limit

explanation.correct: Adaptive Warehouses use a query-based billing model where cost depends on factors like the amount of compute and software resources each query uses.

distractors.A: There is no fixed hourly rate; billing is per-query based on actual resources consumed.
distractors.C: Adaptive Warehouses do not use cluster-based billing; they use per-query billing.
distractors.D: Charges occur for all queries, not only when exceeding throughput limits.

questions.scenario: A team creates an interactive materialized view on their interactive table to speed up a common aggregation query.
questions.stem: Which TWO requirements must be met for the interactive materialized view to work correctly? (Select TWO)

options.text: Both the materialized view and base interactive table must be added to the same interactive warehouse
The materialized view must include a JOIN with at least one other table
The CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW command must include the INTERACTIVE keyword
The materialized view must be smaller than 100GB
The base table must have a PRIMARY KEY defined

explanation.correct: Interactive materialized views require the INTERACTIVE keyword in CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW, and both the view and its base interactive table must be added to the same interactive warehouse.

distractors.B: Joins are NOT supported in materialized views, whether interactive or standard.
distractors.D: There is no documented 100GB size limit for interactive materialized views.
distractors.E: No PRIMARY KEY is required on the base table.

questions.scenario: An Adaptive Warehouse is disabled due to a resource monitor action. The administrator wants to check why it was disabled.
questions.stem: Which TWO columns in the SHOW WAREHOUSES output are specific to Adaptive Warehouses? (Select TWO)

options.text: SCALING_POLICY
WAREHOUSE_SIZE
MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL
DISABLED_REASONS
MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT

explanation.correct: DISABLED_REASONS and MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL are columns specific to Adaptive Warehouses in SHOW WAREHOUSES output.

distractors.A: SCALING_POLICY is a standard/multi-cluster warehouse property, shown as NULL for Adaptive Warehouses.
distractors.B: WAREHOUSE_SIZE applies to standard warehouses and is shown as NULL for Adaptive Warehouses.
distractors.E: MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT is a multi-cluster warehouse property, not specific to Adaptive.

questions.scenario: A developer creates an interactive table with TARGET_LAG = '20 minutes' and specifies both WAREHOUSE and INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE.
questions.stem: What is the purpose of specifying a separate INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE?

options.text: To run queries against the interactive table during initial setup
To handle the initial refresh which often processes more data, allowing use of a larger warehouse
To serve as a failover warehouse if the primary warehouse fails
To run DDL commands required during table creation

explanation.correct: INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE runs the initial refresh on a separate (typically larger) warehouse since initial refreshes often process more data than ongoing maintenance refreshes.

distractors.A: Queries run through an interactive warehouse, not the initialization warehouse.
distractors.C: INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE is not a failover mechanism; it handles only the first refresh.
distractors.D: DDL commands use the standard warehouse context, not a separate initialization warehouse.

questions.stem: Which THREE operations are NOT supported on interactive tables? (Select THREE)

options.text: Adding a row access policy
Creating streams on the table
Using the table as a source for a dynamic table
UPDATE and DELETE DML commands
Renaming the table with ALTER TABLE
Querying with Time Travel

explanation.correct: Interactive tables do not support DML commands like UPDATE/DELETE, cannot be used with streams, and cannot serve as the source for a dynamic table.

distractors.A: Row access policies can be added to interactive tables via ALTER TABLE.
distractors.E: Renaming an interactive table with ALTER TABLE is supported.
distractors.F: Time Travel can be used with interactive tables.

questions.scenario: During property conversion from a standard warehouse to Adaptive, the system automatically computes MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL and QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER.
questions.stem: Which property of the original standard warehouse does the system use to derive the Adaptive Warehouse settings?

options.text: Only the warehouse size
Only MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT and SCALING_POLICY
Warehouse size, MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT, QAS scale factor, and warehouse generation
The number of queries processed in the last 24 hours

explanation.correct: The system derives Adaptive properties from the original warehouse size, MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT (for multi-cluster), QAS scale factor, and warehouse generation (hardware/software generation).

distractors.A: Warehouse size alone is insufficient; multi-cluster settings and QAS configuration are also factored in.
distractors.B: Warehouse size and generation are also used, not just cluster count and scaling policy.
distractors.D: Query history is not used to derive the initial Adaptive Warehouse properties.
